title: graph-server history: Graph, GraphNode, GraphEdge
description:
Design: docs/design/object-history.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: H17. Crates: jmap-graph-types, jmap-graph-server. Size: M.

Scope per decision 5, as confirmed in D1. Spec: object-history-03 §3, §4, §5.1; draft-atwood-jmap-graph-00 (Graph destroy cascades to nodes and edges, node destroy to edges; an edge always connects two existing nodes); graph-edit-00 §Snapshots, §Compaction (ops die with their node); graph-provenance-00 §Retraction (history of a retracted record SHOULD be removed); graph-projection-00. Design: docs/design/object-history.md §2, §7, §9 graph bullet, §12 Q4 (resolved in D1).

Work:
- impl HistoryObject for Graph, GraphNode, GraphEdge (not GraphNodeOp).
- _set_impl split; history handlers for all three, which all have /query.
- register_graph_handlers_with_history. register_graph_edit_handlers is unchanged.
- Memory:
  - record cascades
  - rights_changed_at per Graph
  - GraphNode blob rule (decision 6(d))
  - nodes of a projected Graph keep no history and return the live version only
  - restoring an edited GraphNode follows D1's ruling (recommended: the log restarts empty with head at snapshotSeq)
  - document the provenance retraction purge on the Bk contract
- An edge restore with a destroyed endpoint ⇒ invalidProperties; it succeeds after a GraphNode/set restore earlier in the request.
- Registry cross-check test.

Acceptance:
- Cascade destroys appear in includeDestroyed.
- Edge restore: fails with the endpoint destroyed, succeeds after the node restore.
- Projected node ⇒ live version only.
- GraphNodeOp history flag ⇒ invalidArguments.
- The edited-node restore behaves per D1.
- CHANGELOG, public-api.
